ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The x(t) on the left in the figure is a positive triangular wave, with support interval from t=-2 to t=2, reaching a peak value of 1 at t=0. The y(t) on the right is a negative triangular wave, with support interval from t=-2 to t=0, reaching a minimum value of -1 at t=-1. Reasoning: Compress the time axis of x(t) by a factor of 2 to get x(2t), and its Fourier transform is W(f)=\frac{1}{2}X(f/2). To move the peak position from 0 to -1, let w(t)=x(2t), then y(t)=-w(t+1)=-w(t-(-1)). A time shift left by 1 corresponds to multiplication by e^{j2\pi f} in the frequency domain, and the negative sign comes from amplitude flipping. Therefore Y(f)=-\frac{1}{2}X(f/2)e^{j2\pi f}.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: x(t) is a positive triangle on [-2,2] peaking at 1 at t=0, while y(t) is a negative triangle on [-2,0] reaching -1 at t=-1. Match the vertices to obtain y(t)=-x(2(t+1)). Let w(t)=x(2t), so W(f)=1/2 X(f/2). Since y(t)=-w(t+1)=-w(t-(-1)), the time shift contributes e^{j2πf}; the negative amplitude contributes a minus sign. Therefore Y(f)=-(1/2)X(f/2)e^{j2πf}.
